subject: Control scope tradeoffs and attestation plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Control scope tradeoffs and attestation approach

Team —

We have two parallel drivers coming in: a hard ask from Acme (security team request) that wants FedRAMP-like control evidence for their procurement review, and our ISO 27001 audit we booked for Q1 2027. I sketched a short tradeoff matrix in the attached control-scope-proposal.xlsx and pushed a working doc to Drive (link below).

Two high-level paths:
- ISO-first (broader, lighter evidence, faster attestation for cert) — good for customers focused on ISMS but may not satisfy FedRAMP-specific sampling and cloud boundary evidence.
- FedRAMP-first (narrow, deeper evidence for cloud controls / logging / configuration) — higher engineering lift, but covers more of Acme's ask and customers needing federal-style controls.

Questions for this thread:
1) Which path minimizes overall customer blocker risk while keeping the ISO schedule intact?
2) For FedRAMP-specific asks (sampling windows, continuous logging, KMS proof), who can commit to evidence extraction by the end of the month?
3) Can we produce a canary evidence set auditors can review within 3 weeks (minimal, representative artifacts)?

Proposed owners in the spreadsheet but please confirm or reassign: Jonas — network & VPC controls; Marissa — IAM/SSO artifacts; Mina — logging/observability extracts. Neha, can you comment on SOC 2 attestation overlap (we may be able to reuse some artifacts)?

Attachments: control-scope-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-control-scope-draft

Can everyone reply with a short "OK: owner / ETA" by EOD 2026-10-29 so I can lock the sprint plan.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control scope tradeoffs and attestation approach

Irene —

Quick take:
- ISO-first keeps our certification calendar stable and gives marketing a clean milestone. However, it won't fully satisfy Acme's procurement SOW if they insist on FedRAMP-like evidence (sampling/proof of continuous monitoring).
- Suggest a hybrid sprint: prioritize a FedRAMP-lite canary for Acme (network boundary, KMS config, a 7-day logging extract) while continuing ISO control mapping in parallel. That will reduce the immediate sales blocker and preserve ISO scope.

Owner confirmations (short):
- Jonas: network/VPC boundary can deliver initial diagrams + VPC flow logs extract by 2026-10-29.
- Marissa: will pull IAM role inventories and SSO audit logs; ETA 2026-10-31 for initial package.
- Mina: can extract logging slices (7-day) and retention summary; ETA 2026-10-29.

SOC 2 overlap: yes — a subset of these artifacts (access logs, IAM inventory, change-control evidence) will map to SOC 2 criteria. I recommend we tag artifacts with both ISO and SOC2 references in the spreadsheet (I can do that).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, GRC

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control scope tradeoffs and attestation approach

Thanks — a few clarifying points from IAM side:

- For FedRAMP-style evidence they usually ask for explicit role-to-permission mappings and a sample of recent policy changes plus approval evidence. We can pull role inventories and a policy-change log extract; confirm if a 90-day sample is needed or if 30 days suffices for the canary.
- Also, note our retention policy for auth logs is 13 months (complies with ISO), but extracts for FedRAMP reviewers often need a verified chain (timestamps, storage hashes). I'll attach a short extract explaining formats we can produce.

Attachment: log-retention-extract.txt (txt)

My ask: if the canary aims to cover a customer procurement committee, 30 days with signed metadata and context notes should be fine. If it's a pre-audit for a FedRAMP low-baseline, plan on 90 days. Which one do we want?

-Marissa
Manager, Security Compliance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control scope tradeoffs and attestation approach

I'm aligned with the hybrid plan. Operational notes:

- I'll produce the VPC boundary diagram, Flow Logs sample (7-day + 30-day) and KMS key rotation proof by 2026-10-29. We will tag artifacts in the Drive spreadsheet with a JIRA link for traceability (SUP-3421).
- Proposed sprint: Week 1 (10/26–11/1): collect canary artifacts; Week 2: packaging & reviewer notes; Week 3: dry-run with BrightShore (auditor).

Owners and short ETAs (confirming):
- Jonas: network artifacts (10/29)
- Marissa: IAM + policy change extracts (10/31)
- Mina: logging slices + retention proof (10/29)
- Neha: artifact mapping to SOC2/ISO (10/30)

If everyone confirms I will create the JIRA tasks and link them to SUP-3421.

Jonas Weber
Senior Cloud Security Engineer
